379YE Summer Solstice Announcements by t.d: The Crystal Architect of the Spires announced his intention to create the Storm Vault, a mana sinecure overseen by the Custodian of the Storm Vault. The project cost 10 wains of mithril and 2 crowns per wain in labour, with no upkeep. Tiberius EchoStorm provided the 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns after the Summer Solstice. When complete, the Vault automatically creates the Imperial title of Custodian of the Storm Vault, a Urizen national position appointed by unanimous decision of the Urizen senators and held for life or until revoked.

n.Urizen: Urizen gains a new national title, the Custodian of the Storm Vault, which its senators will appoint by unanimous decision once the sinecure is complete.

t.Zenith: The Storm Vault mana sinecure is to be constructed in Zenith, with the materials and labour costs paid by Tiberius EchoStorm.

r.Zenith/Proceris: Proceris was chosen as the site of the Storm Vault, the mana sinecure commissioned by the Crystal Architect of the Spires.

379YE Summer Solstice Imperial elections.d: Senators were returned for Feroz, Astolat, Weirwater, Bastion, Sarvos, Mitwold, Miaren, Redoubt, Karov and Sermersuaq. Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar became Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy and Kellua Itsepainen of Wintermark became Imperial Consul. Ten generals were appointed to lead armies including the Red Wind Corsairs, Golden Sun, Granite Pillar and Citadel Guard. In the Synod, cardinals and gatekeepers of Courage and Wisdom were chosen, and Severin Teyhard von Holberg of the League became Imperial Inquisitor. Kyra of Halcyon Spire became Grandmaster of the Order of the Unfettered Mind. Bourse seats including the Arratan Gamble, Damatian Cliffs, Night Quarry and Sutton Stone Quarries were allocated, the most expensive going for 405 Thrones.

n.Dawn: Dawn's territories of Astolat and Weirwater returned Earl Gregoire De Gauvain and Valentin Ivarovich Orzel as senators, and Abaddon De Rondell of Dawn became Cardinal of Wisdom.
n.Highguard: Solomon was elected Senator for Bastion, and Asher of Felix's Watch in Highguard became Cardinal of Courage.
n.Navarr: Llewellyn Leafstalker was elected Senator for Miaren, Navarr's only territory named in these elections.
n.The Brass Coast: Liythos i Purjo i Guerra was elected Senator for Feroz, and Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra became Mistress of the Glass Parador.
n.The League: Mirislav was elected Senator for Sarvos, and Severin Teyhard von Holberg of the League was named Imperial Inquisitor.
n.The Marches: Bridget Eastville was elected Senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
n.Urizen: Probus of Shattered Spire was elected Senator for Redoubt, and Livia Cascade of Urizen became Gatekeeper of Wisdom.
n.Varushka: Maximov Strascovich was elected Senator for Karov, Agnieszka Katrinova Prochnost of Varushka became Gatekeeper of Courage, and Zlatimir Prochnost took the Granites of Veltsgorsk.
n.Wintermark: Atte was elected Senator for Sermersuaq, Kellua Itsepainen of Wintermark became Imperial Consul, and Joakim of Wintermark took the Brilliant Shore.

t.Astolat: Earl Gregoire De Gauvain was elected to represent Astolat in the Senate.
t.Bastion: Solomon was elected to represent Bastion in the Senate.
t.Feroz: Liythos i Purjo i Guerra was elected to represent Feroz in the Senate.
t.Karov: Maximov Strascovich was elected to represent Karov in the Senate.
t.Miaren: Llewellyn Leafstalker was elected to represent Miaren in the Senate.
t.Mitwold: Bridget Eastville was elected Senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Redoubt: Probus of Shattered Spire was elected to represent Redoubt in the Senate.
t.Sarvos: Mirislav was elected to represent Sarvos in the Senate.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte was elected to represent Sermersuaq in the Senate.
t.Weirwater: Valentin Ivarovich Orzel was elected to represent Weirwater in the Senate.

379YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: Four civil servants were murdered before the summit. Delegations converged on Anvil: an Asavean Tarquinius emissary, a Grendel diplomat escorted by a major navy anchored off Feroz, Druj and Thule delegations, orcs from the Barrens crossing Brocéliande, and envoys from the Lasambrian Hills and the Iron Confederacy. Hirak the Huntsmaster announced the Drottningbjotha. The Jotun prepared punitive raids on the Marches, the League and Wintermark. Sickness struck Reikos, Brocéliande's vallorn stirred, Druj-slaughtered slaves' ghosts halted work at the Great Pits of Ennerlund and the Vigilant Swan, the League cities were cursed, Lashonar's heralds unsettled Dawn's soldiers, a treasure was found in Redoubt, and the Seventh Wave fought spring horrors in Casinea.

n.Dawn: Heralds of Lashonar the Loquacious mobbed the Golden Sun with an intoxicating ballad that was affecting Dawn's soldiers, and the situation was likely to escalate if left unchecked.
n.Druj: The Druj sent a diplomatic delegation to Anvil under the protection of the law, while their earlier slaughter of slaves left ghosts haunting Imperial resources and their meddling stirred the vallorn of Brocéliande.
n.Grendel: A major Grendel navy anchored off the southern coast of Feroz, ostensibly as escort for a diplomat coming to negotiate at Anvil, though the threat of violence was palpable.
n.Highguard: The Seventh Wave engaged twisted spring horrors in the Highborn territory of Casinea, and sickness spread among the remaining Highborn population of Reikos.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were about to launch punitive raids across the western border into the Marches, the League and Wintermark, and warned that interference with their conquest of the northern Lasambrian Hills would end the existing peace.
n.Navarr: A group of orcs from the Barrens appeared in the Navarr territory of Brocéliande, apparently bound for Anvil, while the vallorn there thrashed in response to tighter trods and Druj meddling.
n.The Brass Coast: A major Grendel navy dropped anchor off the southern coast of Feroz, posing a palpable threat even as it escorted a diplomat to Anvil.
n.The League: All four League cities were struck by curses harmful to magicians and mana sources, League territories faced impending Jotun raids, and ghosts haunted the Great Pits of Ennerlund in Holberg.
n.Thule: A Thule diplomatic delegation came down from Otkodov to parley with the Empire, and with the Varushkans in particular.
n.Urizen: A Torchbearer and her companion found a treasure with massive implications beneath a shattered tower in Redoubt.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's people were dealing with a number of curses and blessings, and its territories were among the targets of impending Jotun raids.

t.Brocéliande: The vallorn of Brocéliande stirred fitfully in response to tighter trods and Druj meddling, and a group of orcs from the Barrens appeared there on their way to Anvil.
t.Casinea: The Seventh Wave engaged twisted spring horrors in Casinea.
t.Feroz: A major Grendel navy dropped anchor off the southern coast of Feroz, escorting a diplomat but carrying a palpable threat of violence.
t.Holberg: Hate-filled ghosts of slaves slaughtered by the Druj haunted the Great Pits of Ennerlund, preventing progress on reopening the Bourse resource.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Thule delegation to Anvil came down from frozen Otkodov.
t.Redoubt: A Torchbearer and her companion found a treasure with massive implications under a shattered tower in Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Sickness struck Reikos, spreading through both the armies there and the remaining Highborn population.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the orcs who appeared in Brocéliande on their way to Anvil had come out of the Barrens.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Druj slaughter of slaves at the Great Pits of Ennerlund left scores of angry ghosts haunting the mine, preventing all progress on reopening it.

379YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: Karsk stayed in an uneasy peace. In Reikos the Druj withdrew into Urith Barath (High Chalcis), leaving curses, traps and a miasma of dread, before a blood-red storm brought flooding and severe sickness. In Sermersuaq, Imperial forces repelled a Thule assault of over twenty thousand orcs, and Freeborn raids forced the Thule out of the southern Stonefields, at a cost of over a thousand Imperial dead. Jotun raiders were also destroyed. Holberg was liberated as the Druj fled across the river into the Mallum, though the Scorpion Sting lagged behind. A Grendel navy landed in Spiral, overran the Legacy and much of the territory, and demanded Fort Mezudan surrender or retreat.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights of the Hounds of Glory swore to hold the Thule back in Sermersuaq, while the Eastern Sky and Golden Sun fought in Holberg and earned grudging respect from the Knights of Eleonaris.
n.Druj: The Druj abandoned most of Reikos for their citadel at High Chalcis, lost Holberg with around three thousand orcs killed or drowned, and remained engaged by Imperial troops besieging them at Ipotavo in Axos.
n.Grendel: The Grendel landed a fresh army from a red-sailed navy, seized the Legacy and much of Spiral, held captured Urizen children aboard their flagships, and demanded that Fort Mezudan surrender or withdraw.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar pushed into Haros Water in Reikos, and Highborn priests and magisters struggled to keep the spectre of dread in check among the armies.
n.Jotun: Two large Jotun warbands raiding into Stark and the Suaq Wastes were captured and destroyed by Imperial orc patrols, raising fears that the Jotun might join the fighting in Sermersuaq.
n.Navarr: The Quiet Step advanced cautiously in Reikos, its scouts facing Druj curses near Haros, while Navarr priests and vates fought against the dread and investigated the corrupted rain.
n.The League: Holberg was finally liberated after a thirty-year campaign, a day the League is expected to remember for years, though malignant tree spirits still cause destruction.
n.Thule: The Thule stayed silent in Karsk, but their massive assault in Sermersuaq failed, costing them losses reckoned at half again the Empire's and forcing them to cede the southern Stonefields.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost the Legacy in Ossuary and much of Spiral to the Grendel, its magicians captured or killed, its children taken aboard Grendel ships, and Fort Mezudan was given an ultimatum.
n.Varushka: Varushka kept its hold on western Karsk, sent a final mithril delivery from Moresvah and a gift of mithril to Branoc, while the Golden Axe and Varushkan magicians helped turn the tide in Sermersuaq.
n.Wintermark: The Fist of the Mountains refused to cede ground in Sermersuaq, rejoined the Green Shield in fellowship as the curse of tradition broke, and the Winterfolk turned scornful of the Freeborn and their undead allies.

t.Holberg: The Druj were driven out of Holberg across the river into the Mallum, completing its liberation, though about a thousand Scorpion Sting troops still lingered near the river.
t.Karsk: Karsk remained an Imperial territory in a strained peace with the Thule occupying its east, with only minor scouting clashes and a promising harvest for Varushkan farms.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invited the garrison of Fort Mezudan to retreat westward to Redoubt as an alternative to surrender.
t.Reikos: Imperial armies made little progress against Druj curses, traps and pervasive dread before a blood-red storm flooded the territory and brought serious sickness.
t.Sermersuaq: The Empire held its positions for the first time in the war and reclaimed the southern Stonefields, but lost over a thousand troops while the Thule still held the upper passes.
t.Spiral: A Grendel landing and northern offensive overran much of Spiral, with the invaders appearing intent on taking the entire territory.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen sentinels retreated north into Zenith with the few survivors rescued from the Legacy.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: Imperial forces swept from the plains of Ennerlund into the forests to begin the final campaign.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Misericorde was the scene of the campaign's most vicious fighting, with Druj burned out of their bolt-holes before breaking and fleeing across the river.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Mentioned in passing: the Scorpion Sting is described as the remnant of the army that once ruled from the fallen citadel of Rebeshof.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: The once-tamed woods of Utterlund, twisted by Druj magic into hostile thickets of living briars and trees, were one of the final battlefields of the liberation.
r.Karsk/Branoc: Forces loyal to the sovereign of Branoc kept their distance from the Thule, and the people of the Broken Hill received a Varushkan gift of mithril after sharing hospitality with the hillsfolk of Nitrost.
r.Karsk/Lestasny: A twisted fortress of trees watched over Lestasny, young people of Kosti and Veresk spoke of founding a new settlement there, and rumours of husks in its south-western forests came to nothing.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The Malinov, Sloev and Pravin families of Moresvah sent their final delivery of mithril and volunteers to the Northern Eagle before turning to their own concerns.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: The unliving army of the accused faded into the hills of Nitrost and the citadel of ice and bone stood unmelted, its garrison idle as the Thule did not come.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: The Valiant Pegasus and Granite Pillar pushed into Haros Water against curses, poisoned land and traps, but made little real progress before the storms and sickness struck.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule launched a huge assault to seize the last parts of the Silver Peaks they did not control, but the Imperial defences held.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Jotun warbands reaving into Stark were captured and destroyed by Imperial orc patrols.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The Winter Sun tracked and killed Thule raiding parties trying to slip into Suaq Fount to circle the Imperial line.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Probing Jotun raids into the Suaq Wastes were intercepted and destroyed by Imperial orc patrols.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Grendel forces marching from the Legacy re-established uncontested control over Ankra.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The newly landed Grendel army crushed all resistance in Apstrus.
r.Spiral/Apulus: The Grendel navy anchored off Apulus to land thousands of troops, crushed all resistance there, and set surrendered Urizen to building siege engines under the command of Garaigh the Gentle.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Grendel forces re-established uncontested control over Cinion as they advanced towards Fort Mezudan.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: A lightning Grendel strike overwhelmed the token Urizen force at the Legacy, which was plundered and fortified before reinforcements from Fort Mezudan could arrive.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Grendel struck Screed and the Black Plateau in force, rounding up Urizen magicians who were helping those freed from the Plateau's fading influence.

Accept Barrens peace treaty.d: A delegation from the Barrens negotiated a treaty governing the movement of troops through their lands, and the terms were put to the Senate in a motion proposed by Upwold and seconded by Therunin. The motion stated that it did not cover the Navarri army of the Black Thorns moving through the Barrens into Brocéliande, which was to happen whatever the terms. The motion was defeated and the treaty was not accepted. The Barrens delegation had already left Anvil before the vote, and it is unclear whether they know their treaty has been declined.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named. The treaty came from the orcs and humans of the Barrens, a territory listed as held by the Druj that season.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the motion excluded the Black Thorns' march through the Barrens into Brocéliande, stating that it would go ahead regardless of the treaty.
t.The Barrens: The treaty offered by the Barrens orcs and humans to let troops pass through their lands was rejected by the Senate, and the delegation may not yet know it was declined.

Accept Thule peace treaty.d: Under the recorded terms, the Thule would withdraw from Branoc and Crowslook and would not harm any Varushkan, with Varushkans likewise not harming the Thule. The Thule would receive the Silver Peaks, the Empire would withdraw all its forces from there, and the Thule would leave the rest of Sermersuaq. Hostilities would cease for three years, and neither side would invade the other's other controlled regions or raid the other. After a year of the treaty holding, information about the Enemies of the Empire and further trade opportunities would be negotiated. The Thule would also receive a usable ritual script for Crystalline Focus of Aesh, chosen from an approved list.

n.Thule: The Thule gained the Silver Peaks, a usable ritual script for Crystalline Focus of Aesh and three years of peace with the Empire. In return they agreed to leave Branoc, Crowslook and the rest of Sermersuaq and to refrain from invasion and raids.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark lost the Silver Peaks in Sermersuaq to the Thule, with all Imperial forces to withdraw from there. In return, the Thule would leave the rest of the territory and hostilities would cease for three years.

t.Sermersuaq: Under the treaty, Sermersuaq was partitioned: the Silver Peaks passed to the Thule, while the Thule agreed to leave the rest of the territory.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Silver Peaks were ceded to the Thule, and the Empire was to withdraw all its forces from the region.

Archive:379YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.d: The roll named the senator for every Imperial territory and the holders of Senate offices such as the Conscience of the Senate (Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg) and the Imperial Consul (Kellua Itsepainen). The post of Admiral was vacant. It listed every general and army, the Warmage, the cardinals, gatekeepers and virtue inquisitors of the Synod, the archmagi and grandmasters, and Bourse seats with their winning bids. The Great Forest at Reikos remained in Druj hands and would not be auctioned until Reikos was Imperial again. The Great Pits of Ennerlund needed repair before they could be allocated, now that Holberg was Imperial once more.

n.Dawn: Dawn sent senators for Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater, and generals for the Hounds of Glory, Golden Sun and Eastern Sky. Its nobles also held the Pride and Wisdom cardinalships and the Archmage of Autumn's seat.
n.Druj: The Druj still held the Great Forest at Reikos, keeping that Bourse seat out of Imperial auction, and had lost hold of the Great Pits of Ennerlund now that Holberg was Imperial again.
n.Highguard: Highguard returned senators for Bastion, Casinea and Necropolis and generals for the Seventh Wave, Granite Pillar and Valiant Pegasus. Its priests held the Courage, Loyalty and Vigilance cardinalships among many Synod posts.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs fielded generals for the Winter Sun and Summer Storm, and their national Bourse seat, the Steel Fist, was held by Irontide Kul. Quartermaster General Irontide Rad died during the Solstice.
n.Navarr: Navarr returned senators for Hercynia, Miaren and Therunin and generals for the Black Thorns and Quiet Step. Hywel Summercrow served as Chaplain Consular and Idris Eternal held the Thimble.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn returned senators for Feroz, Kahraman, Madruga and Segura and generals for the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South. Karlos i Shartha i Riqueza held the Broken Shore Bounty.
n.The League: The League returned four senators and General Gabriel Barossa of the Wolves of War. Its citizens held the Conscience of the Senate, the Imperial Inquisitor's post, the Ambition cardinalship and the Master of the Imperial Mint.
n.The Marches: The Marches returned senators for Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold and fielded four generals, for the Cullachs, Drakes, Strong Reeds and Bounders. Silent John served as Gatekeeper of Ambition.
n.Urizen: Urizen returned senators for Morrow, Redoubt and Zenith and General Nicassia Avicia of the Citadel Guard. Its citizens held the Loyalty and Wisdom gatekeeperships and the post of High Exorcist.
n.Varushka: Varushka returned senators for Karsk, Karov, Miekarova and Volodmartz and generals for the Northern Eagle and Golden Axe. Its people held the Eternal Shafts of Time, the Granites of Veltsgorsk and the grandmastery of the Shuttered Lantern.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark returned four senators and generals for the Green Shield and Fist of the Mountain, and held the Prosperity and Way cardinalships. Kellua Itsepainen served as Imperial Consul.

t.Astolat: Earl Gregoire De Gauvain sat as senator for Astolat.
t.Bastion: Solomon sat as senator for Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Orrick sat as senator for Bregasland, the Dour Fens.
t.Casinea: Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold sat as senator for Casinea.
t.Feroz: Liythos i Purjo i Guerra sat as senator for Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun sat as senator for Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: Rhain sat as senator for Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Rossalyn Jordan sat as senator for Holberg, which was once again an Imperial territory.
t.Kahraman: Zamira i Covas i Erigo sat as senator for Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Uskolli sat as senator for Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Maximov Strascovich sat as senator for Karov.
t.Karsk: Radomir sat as senator for Karsk.
t.Madruga: Anwar i Del-Toro i Riqueza sat as senator for Madruga.
t.Miaren: Llewellyn Leafstalker sat as senator for Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Dušan Otecovna Zlata sat as senator for Miekarova.
t.Mitwold: Bridget Eastville sat as senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Ariadne sat as senator for Morrow.
t.Necropolis: Adamah of the Silent Tide sat as senator for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Probus of Shattered Spire sat as senator for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: The Great Forest at Reikos remained in Druj hands and would not be auctioned until Reikos was once again an Imperial territory.
t.Sarvos: Mirislav sat as senator for Sarvos.
t.Segura: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra sat as senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Escalados deCarsenere sat as senator for Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte sat as senator for Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Thanmir Hrafn sat as senator for Skarsind.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato sat as senator for Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Gant Archama sat as senator for Temeschwar.
t.Therunin: Caerwyn Summer Crow sat as senator for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Henry Ward sat as senator for Upwold, The Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Irina Kardaova Arkady sat as senator for Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Valentin Ivarovich Orzel sat as senator for Weirwater, and the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat went to Landon of Longridge for 280 Thrones.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund, formerly held by the Druj, needed repairing before they could be allocated now that Holberg was Imperial again.

Bloody murder.d: Calladan of Widow's Walk was killed travelling to Sybella; veteran Douglas Wyrdwatcher was found dead in Canterspire in Morrow; Suaq pacifist Bridget Windsdottir was also slain; and Arnaud di Sarvos, trained at the School of Epistemology in Tassato and a long-serving Synod aide, was found with his throat cut. Each was attacked alone with edged weapons, the scenes deliberately drenched in blood, with no sign of forced entry. With retirements compounding the losses, the Senate's capacity to commission historical research fell permanently from five to two per season, forcing the Minister of Historical Research, the Advisor on the Vallorn and the Dredgemaster of Feverwater to compete with senators. Magistrates continue to investigate; the Senate raised a motion to protect the remaining researchers.

n.The League: Arnaud di Sarvos, a scholar trained at Tassato's School of Epistemology and twenty years an aide to the Synod, was among the slain, and the Empire's research capacity that League senators draw on was sharply cut.
n.Urizen: Douglas Wyrdwatcher was murdered while visiting Canterspire in Urizen-held Morrow, bringing the killings into the nation's lands.

t.Morrow: Veteran researcher Douglas Wyrdwatcher, said to be a man not easily killed, was found murdered while visiting Canterspire in Morrow.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the murdered Arnaud di Sarvos had honed his eye for detail at the School of Epistemology in Tassato.

Blue seas, white stone.d: Alonso Tarquinius, of the powerful Tarquinius family and agent of Lady Madrianna of the Blue Stones, trade advisor to the Asavean Plenum, arrived at Sarvos aboard Tarquinius trading ships crewed by free sailors. A Plenum galley escorted them and anchored half a mile out, reportedly because its oars were worked by slaves. Alonso stayed at the Asavean embassy before visiting Anvil, seeking to meet the Imperial Ambassador to Asavea and perhaps representatives of the Synod. With peace between the Archipelago and the Empire, he was protected by and bound to Imperial law. His experiences could sway the Plenum for or against the Empire. In the event, his visit was marred by curses from Imperial citizens, leaving future relations uncertain.

n.The League: The League's great port received the Asavean envoy and his cargo of white granite, its free guilder dockworkers unloading the stone and collecting dock fees, while Alonso formed an unflattering first impression of the League folk as industrious but uncouth.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Asavean ships and their Plenum warship escort sighted an orc vessel as they rounded the coast into the Bay of Catazar, but completed their passage safely.
t.Sarvos: Two Tarquinius trading vessels unloaded white granite on the Sarvos docks, Alonso Tarquinius lodged at the Asavean embassy in the City of Jewels, and a reputedly slave-rowed Asavean galley lay at anchor half a mile offshore.

Construct College of Summer Magic.d: Proposed by Miaren, the motion sought permission, but no funding, to build a College of Magic dedicated to Cathan Canae. Because it followed the Eternal's designs, its cost differed from a standard college: 90 wains of white granite, 30 of mithril and 30 of weirwood, 35 Thrones of labour and a year to build, with upkeep of 25 Thrones. Llewellyn Leafstalker supplied all of the materials and labour between Autumn 379YE and Spring 380YE. The college was built at Volchitrava in Miekarova and named The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun. Its completion created the title of Master of Ice and Darkness, which the senator made an Imperial position assigned by declaration of the Conclave.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained an Imperial College of Summer Magic on its soil, along with the Master of Ice and Darkness title, which is assigned by Conclave declaration.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova became home to The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, a Summer college built at Volchitrava to the designs of Cathan Canae.

r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: The map attaches the college to Srodkoja; the page itself gives the site as Volchitrava in Miekarova, where The Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun was completed.

Construct Commonwealth embassy.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa, the motion called for an embassy to the Commonwealth to be constructed in Madruga. It passed in principle, but no money was set aside for it. The commission required 25 wains each of weirwood and white granite, 12 thrones of labour and one season to build, with upkeep of 5 thrones. After the Winter Solstice of 379YE, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason supplied the full materials and the labour cost. Completing the embassy automatically creates the Imperial title of Ambassador to the Commonwealth.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast was to host the Empire's embassy to the Commonwealth on its own soil in Madruga, giving the nation a direct diplomatic stake in relations with the Commonwealth.

t.Madruga: Madruga was chosen as the site of the Commonwealth embassy, with the materials and labour for it supplied after the Winter Solstice of 379YE.

Construct Garden of Falling Snow.d: The motion proposed building the Garden of Falling Snow in Hahnmark at no cost to the Senate. It is a sinecure that supplies additional herbs, and its holder, the Gatekeeper of Falling Snow, is to be appointed by unanimous vote of Wintermark's senators. The motion gave neither the size nor the exact location of the sinecure, leaving both for the senator to decide, with standard costs applying. After the Summer Solstice 379YE, Hengest Dun of Wintermark supplied 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns. Construction was completed, creating a Wintermark national Imperial title.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a new national Imperial title, the Gatekeeper of Falling Snow, whose holder is chosen by unanimous vote of its senators. The garden was built with weirwood and crowns supplied by Hengest Dun.

t.Hahnmark: The Garden of Falling Snow, a herb garden sinecure, was built in Hahnmark. Its exact location within the territory was left for the senator to decide.

Construct apothecary clearing house in T.d: The motion called for funds to construct a ministry in Tassato to purchase herbs for making medicinal potions for Imperial warriors. It passed in principle and was costed at 42 Thrones. It did not set the ministry's size, location or how its holder would be chosen, leaving those choices to the proposing senator. After the Spring Equinox 380YE, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato provided 12 wains of weirwood for the work. The clearing house was completed in Mestra in Tassato, and the Imperial title of Master of the Clearing House was made a League national appointment.

n.The League: The League gained a new Imperial title, Master of the Clearing House, which became a League national appointment. Weirwood for the building came from Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato.

t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the apothecary clearing house was built in Mestra, giving the territory a ministry for buying herbs for the Empire's medicines.

Crossroads.d: Across the Empire, runecasters kept drawing Gralm (the Crossroads), Ull (the Coin) and the blank twenty-seventh rune. League troupes found themselves staging the Prince and the Witch. Urizen astronomancers read a conjunction of the Wanderer with the hidden Stork, the sign of making the right choice for the right reasons. While the conjunction lasted, Signs and Portents, Whispering Shadow Courtiers and Dreams in the Witch House rose in magnitude by two. Call Winged Messenger, The Ambassadorial Gatekeeper and The Ethereal Courier fell by two, and green iron could stand in for crystal mana at two measures to one. Sensitive characters dreamt of crossroads, games of chance, ravens and spiders. The effects faded within a month of the Summer Solstice.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Stork's meaning is likened to what Highguard calls the Decision to be Virtuous.
n.Urizen: Urizen astronomancers and Hakima watched the Summer skies and saw a falling star, a crimson tear of the Phoenix, come to earth somewhere in Urizen's mountains. They traced the true sign to a conjunction of the Wanderer with the hidden Stork, the right choice made for the right reasons.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark runecasting carried the omen first, with Gralm, Ull and the blank rune appearing again and again. The page's vignette shows a Wintermark mystic telling a young Grimnir that his choice will shape his life but must be made alone.

t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: in the opening vignette, a young Grimnir's fateful choice is whether to go south or stay in Skarsind.

Disburse funds for Summer college.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Karsk, the motion asked for 100 Thrones to buy materials for the ongoing construction of a Summer college. The motion itself said it did not matter whether the college was in Urizen or Navarr. The page notes that the Senate had already commissioned two such colleges, one in Morrow and one in Miekarova. The motion passed at a cost of 100 Thrones, and the money was disbursed to the senator for Miekarova.

n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the motion named Navarr as one of two possible locations for the Summer college, saying the choice did not matter.
n.Urizen: Urizen was named in the motion as a possible home for the Summer college, and its territory of Morrow was the site of one of the two colleges the Senate had commissioned.
n.Varushka: Varushkan senators drove the motion: Miekarova proposed it and Karsk seconded it, and the 100 Thrones went to the Miekarova senator for a college the Senate had commissioned in Miekarova.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova's senator proposed the motion and received the 100 Thrones, and the territory was the site of one of the two Summer colleges the Senate had commissioned.
t.Morrow: Morrow was the site of one of the two Summer colleges the Senate had commissioned, though the funds from this motion went to the senator for Miekarova.

Golden Sails.d: A Grendel navy roughly equivalent in strength to an Imperial army anchored south of Shantarim and the Isle of Osseni, too large for individual fleets to challenge. It escorted a single weirwood trading vessel carrying a Grendel diplomat and a small honour guard. The Grendel were furious that the Empire had kept raiding their ships in the Bay of Catazar despite agreeing a cessation of hostilities, having hoped the Jotun threat on their border would bring the Empire to a profitable accord. The diplomat travelled via Sarvos under Freeborn escort and was protected by the law of delegation protection. Ambassador Cartok was received at Anvil, where a peace treaty was discussed; he returned to Feroz without incident and the fleet sailed south.

n.Grendel: The Grendel sent a massive war fleet as a pointed show of force to escort their ambassador Cartok, demanding an end to Imperial raiding of their ships, and discussed a peace treaty at Anvil before sailing home.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the growing Jotun threat on the Grendel border is cited as a reason the Grendel hoped the Empire would agree to an accord.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn of Feroz were alarmed by a Grendel war fleet anchored off their coast that could threaten the whole territory, while Freeborn vessels escorted the Grendel diplomat onward towards Anvil.
n.The League: The Grendel diplomat's ship passed safely through League waters via Sarvos on its way to Anvil.

t.Bay of Catazar: Continued Imperial raiding of Grendel shipping in the bay, despite an agreed cessation of hostilities, provoked the Grendel show of force, and the Grendel warned that the bay was not safe.
t.Feroz: A Grendel navy roughly equivalent to an Imperial army anchored south of Shantarim and the Isle of Osseni, posing a serious potential threat until it sailed south after the diplomat's return.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn girl in Feroz mistook the Grendel fleet for the new navy being built in Madruga, still at least six months from completion.
t.Sarvos: The Grendel diplomat's route to Anvil took him through Sarvos under Freeborn escort.

Green and pleasant lands.d: The envoys claimed to represent the two great clans of the independent orcs east of the Empire, which reportedly threw off Druj rule over Winter 377YE. They were led by a shaman of the Great Forest clan and a warrior of the Black Wind clan, with evident tensions between them, and accompanied by a human of strong briar lineage. They were encouraged chiefly by the Senate's Spring decision to recognise them as foreigners rather than barbarians, so they came under the protection of the law, not delegation protection. A herald of Lashonar led them into Greenstead; members of the Splitroot Striding escorted them by the trods to Anvil. There they negotiated a treaty that was discussed in the Senate, then returned safely to the Barrens.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of the Barrens are reported to have thrown off the oppressive chains of the Druj over Winter 377YE.
n.Navarr: Navarr guardians met the orc delegation in Brocéliande, and after much discussion members of the Splitroot Striding agreed to escort the envoys along the trods to Anvil, leaving the Navarr likely to be the first to hear of their approach.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the orcs carried an invitation from the Wintermark senator Jorma Steelhail, one of the factors behind their journey.

t.Brocéliande: The orc envoys emerged unannounced into Brocéliande under a flag of truce and were led into Greenstead by a herald of Lashonar before being handed over to Navarr guides.
t.The Barrens: The independent orc clans of the Barrens, said to have freed themselves from the Druj, sent their first peaceful envoys to the Empire, and the delegation returned there safely after negotiating a treaty at Anvil.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell was where the band of orcs from the Barrens first appeared without warning, flying a flag of truce.

Little boats.d: A year after a Druj delegation from Reikos fared badly before the Senate, three crude boats with bile-yellow sails crossed the Semmerlak. A swimmer bearing a flag marked with the rune of Lann declared they came in peace to discuss an end to hostilities. Two boats came ashore with a small band of diplomats; the third stayed at anchor beyond bowshot, silent but not hostile, watched by Lacre's yeofolk. The Druj invoked the law of delegation protection, which the Constitutional Court held protects them at Anvil as if they were citizens, and asked the Dawnish to keep them safe. At Anvil they negotiated extensively, the Senate discussed a proposed peace treaty, and the Druj went home unharmed.

n.Dawn: The Druj landed on Dawnish shores, praised the honour of the people of the rising sun, and asked Dawn to escort them to Anvil and protect them as guests under Imperial law.
n.Druj: The Druj sent a second delegation under a flag of truce to discuss terms for peace with the Senate; it negotiated at Anvil and returned safely to the Mallum.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page; it is attached only through the map.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page; it is attached only through the map.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the previous year's Druj delegation is said to have come from Reikos.
t.Semmerholm: The Druj boats approached the shore east of Lacre, where the yeofolk raised the town and the delegation landed before setting out for Anvil.
t.The Semmerlak: The Druj crossed the lake from the Mallum in three small boats, and one stayed at anchor offshore, refusing all communication but showing no hostility.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls the Druj attack on Weirwater across the Semmerlak during the reign of Empress Varkula, the last attack in force across the lake.

r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Yeofolk working the shore east of Lacre spotted the Druj boats and received the delegation, then kept day-and-night watch on the boat left at anchor.

Lonely, dark and deep.d: After Drefa, Voice of the Quiet Forest, led the Dance of Navarr and Thorn for a third time, the vallorn stirred and vallornspawn attacked settlements on the forest's edge. The remaining Druj in Elerael pulled back to Reikos, leaving the region open either to vallorn expansion or to an Imperial army that could take it with little resistance. After the Summer Solstice, miasma and bands of ettercaps spread into Casinea, Astolat and Semmerholm. The ettercaps were swiftly dealt with and the miasma soon dissipated, but over the following month a quarter of farm and forest produce in those territories emerged twisted. Most was burned, but magisters found some of the fruit could serve like crystal mana in Spring rituals.

n.Dawn: Astolat and Semmerholm suffered miasma and ettercap attacks, and a quarter of their farm and forest produce was twisted, though Dawnish knights and yeomen helped drive off the creatures.
n.Druj: The Druj abandoned Elerael and fell back to Reikos, apparently with more knowledge of the vallorn than other orcs, though it is unknown whether they provoked it.
n.Highguard: Casinea's borders with Brocéliande were struck by miasma and ettercaps, and a quarter of its farm and forest produce emerged twisted and strange.
n.Navarr: Navarr's repeated expansion of the trods, led by Drefa of the Quiet Forest, appears to be weakening the vallorn, which lashed out in response; Thorns fought vallornspawn emerging from the Black Boughs.

t.Astolat: Miasma and ettercaps spread into Astolat from the forest, and a quarter of its farm and forest produce was transformed, some usable in Spring magic.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn within Brocéliande shifted restlessly and loosed vallornspawn and miasma on its surroundings, seemingly in reaction to the repaired trods draining its power.
t.Casinea: Casinea's border farms and forests endured miasma and ettercap attacks, with a quarter of their produce twisted into unnatural forms.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Druj remaining in Elerael were withdrawing to Reikos.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm was touched by the spreading miasma and ettercaps, and a quarter of its farm and forest produce, including orchards and butterflies, emerged strange and misshapen.

r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: Vallornspawn stumbled out of the Black Boughs to attack nearby steadings, where Thorns rallied to repel them.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: The Druj left Elerael unoccupied, giving the restless vallorn an easy chance to expand there, or an Imperial army the opportunity to claim it with minimal resistance.

News from the north.d: With the crown recovered and Erkenbrand crowned champion, the threat of Wintermark tearing apart passed, though the Thule sorcerer behind the curse escaped. In Sermersuaq the ritual Winter's Ghosts cut all production by a quarter, amid sightings of sinister spirits; the curse later ran its course. Kallavesi mana sites remained halved. Auras of Prosperity raised mine output and congregation influence in Hahnmark and Skarsind while hurting businesses. In Skarsind, news that Wintermark would give the territory to the Imperial Orcs caused anger, and miners began stripping their mines with no maintenance. Freeborn intelligence warned of major Jotun attacks on western Kallavesa.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: a Steinr pilgrim travels to Emperor Guntherm's tomb in Necropolis, and rumour vaguely blames the Highborn, through the Young Empress, for the draining of Kallavesi mana.
n.Imperial Orcs: Wintermark's decision to give Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs as a homeland was celebrated at Anvil, but some Skarsind miners began stripping their mines so that the incoming orcs would not profit from their work.
n.Jotun: Jotun raiders struck along Wintermark's western borders into Stark, the Suaq Wastes, Westmark and Skymarsh, and Freeborn intelligence pointed to major Jotun attacks on western Kallavesa in the months ahead.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the tale is set in a Navarr wayhouse, where a Suaq hunter travelling with a striding hears the northern news over Navarr beer.
n.Thule: The Thule kept fighting for the Silver Peaks and laid the curse Winter's Ghosts on Sermersuaq, while the Thule sorcerer behind the Bane of Tradition escaped.
n.Wintermark: The Bane of Tradition faded with the crown's recovery and Erkenbrand's crowning, but Wintermark's homelands suffered curses, Jotun raids, and anger in Skarsind at its senators' decision to give the territory away.

t.Hahnmark: Auras of Prosperity sharply increased mine profits and congregation influence while hurting other businesses, and there was talk of building a great shrine or cathedral to Prosperity to keep the mines blessed.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesi mana sites stayed at half production under a lingering curse, and the Freeborn warned of major Jotun attacks on western Kallavesa after raids into Westmark and Skymarsh.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: a Steinr woman is travelling to Necropolis on pilgrimage to the tomb of Emperor Guntherm.
t.Sermersuaq: Winter's Ghosts cut all production in the territory by a quarter, bringing crop failure, sickness, fires, floods and an angry mammoth herd, before the curse ran its course; icewalkers feared these spirits might combine dangerously with husk-raising magic.
t.Skarsind: Many felt betrayed by the decision to give Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs, and as the Prosperity auras lingered, miners neglected maintenance to strip their mines, threatening to leave them unsafe.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Mystics reported eerie dancing lights over the Kallavesa Marsh and muttered grimly about what they might portend.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule continued to fight Imperial forces for control of the Silver Peaks.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Jotun reavers raided into Stark but were driven off by the armies in Sermersuaq.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Jotun raiders reached as far as the Suaq Wastes before the armies in Sermersuaq drove them off.

Promises to keep.d: A small Thule party, led by a spellbinder and accompanied by armoured warriors and an apparent slave, approached the vale of Wendell's Hope near Coldmere. The schlacta at first refused them, but the spellbinder swore an oath of peace in the name of Orobus the Chained before witnesses, and the gates were opened. The Thule sought to address the Varushkans at Anvil and the Senate, and perhaps the Conclave, to discuss borders between Otkodov and the Empire and a possible end to hostilities. They were escorted south through Karov, then by Delev wardens. Protected under the law of delegations, they negotiated at Anvil, a peace treaty went before the Senate, and they returned safely to Otkodov.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page and plays no stated part in the Thule delegation.
n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov sent a spellbinder-led embassy under oath to Orobus the Chained to negotiate borders and a cessation of hostilities, leading to a peace treaty being presented to the Senate before the delegation returned home safely.
n.Varushka: Varushkans guarded, received and escorted the Thule envoys from vale to vale, and were expected to be the first at Anvil to learn of their arrival and to hear their offer of peace and borders.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page and has no stated role in the events.
t.Karov: The Thule delegation was passed south through Karov by Varushkan escorts on its way to Anvil.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the Thule spellbinder invoked what the people of Karsk would say if the schlacta turned the envoys away.
t.Miekarova: The Thule envoys arrived at Wendell's Hope in Miekarova, where the schlacta first refused them before opening the gates once the spellbinder swore an oath of peace beneath Miekarova's trees.
t.Otkodov: The Thule-held territory was the source of the delegation, which sought agreed borders between Otkodov and the Empire and returned there safely after the talks.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: The Thule party descended through the woods of Mieriada to Coldmere and the vale of Wendell's Hope, where the parley at the gates and the spellbinder's oath took place.

Raise Towerjacks army.d: The motion permitted the League to restore the Towerjacks, an army incorporating many siege experts, under special circumstances that differed from the standard costs of raising an Imperial army. It passed in principle and at 200 Thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Holberg. Construction required 125 mithril and six months, with upkeep of 50 Thrones per season. Ros Jordan supplied 65 wains of mithril after the Summer Solstice and 60 wains after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, providing the full 125. The army will muster in Holberg, and once it is raised it will automatically create the Imperial title of General.

n.The League: The League regains the Towerjacks, a siege-expert army of its own, along with a new Imperial General's title, at a cost of 125 mithril and ongoing upkeep of 50 Thrones a season.

t.Holberg: Holberg's senator seconded the motion and received the 200 Thrones, and the restored Towerjacks will muster in Holberg.

Reikos flux.d: Two weeks before the Summer solstice the Valiant Pegasus was struck by a terrible disease of exhaustion, diarrhoea and vomiting that killed many, and the Granite Pillar and Quiet Step soon followed. Affected armies were expected to lose one in ten soldiers each season, and resources in Reikos were to produce only three quarters of normal output; any army leaving would spread it. After the solstice the Granite Pillar and Quiet Step withdrew, the flux burnt from them by rituals of Day, while the Valiant Pegasus remained exposed. During the Autumn Equinox a herbal cure was found, and Spring magic focused through the Urizen Citadel Guard brought cleansing rain that cured the armies and citizens of Reikos.

n.Druj: The Druj appeared to be falling back before the Highborn advance in Reikos, and the Empire suspected the plague might be a malignant Druj scheme to drive the Imperial armies out.
n.Urizen: The Urizen army, the Citadel Guard, served as the focus for the Spring magic that filled Reikos at the Autumn Equinox and washed away the flux.

t.Reikos: Reikos was ravaged by the flux, its inhabitants and property suffering alongside the Imperial armies there, with resources cut to three quarters of normal output until cleansing Spring rain cured the territory at the Autumn Equinox.

Shadow in the west.d: Jotun raids, rumoured to be intensifying at the Spring Equinox, hit Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold, the lands around Meade and Tassato, and halls in western Sermersuaq and Kallavesa. Imperial armies in Sermersuaq destroyed two warbands. The units at Fort Braydon in Kahraman, reinforced by crystal warriors under Anwar i Del Toro i Riqueza, caught a Jotun scout who revealed that probing attacks on Mitwold and Kahraman would continue while major raids targeted Kallavesa, Bregasland, Upwold and Tassato. These threatened heavy losses of production there. The Red Wind Corsairs, Winter Sun, Fist of the Mountains and Hounds of Glory were sent to these four territories and blunted the raids through several skirmishes. Historians warned such raids often precede war.

n.Jotun: Jotun warbands raided across the Imperial border from the Mournwold, lost two warbands in Sermersuaq and a captured scout. Their planned major raids were then blunted by the Imperial armies sent against them.
n.The Brass Coast: Fort Braydon's garrison in Kahraman, aided by crystal warriors under Anwar i Del Toro i Riqueza, intercepted the Jotun scout whose interrogation revealed the enemy's plans.
n.The League: The lands around Tassato were plagued by raids, and the city's territory was named as a target for major Jotun raids that threatened all its production before the Hounds of Glory were sent to defend it.
n.The Marches: Marcher farmsteads in Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold were raided, and Bregasland and Upwold faced major raids threatening their production until Imperial armies were sent there.
n.Wintermark: Jotun attacked halls in western Sermersuaq and Kallavesa. Imperial armies wiped out two warbands in Sermersuaq, while Kallavesa faced major raids until the Red Wind Corsairs defended it.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland farmsteads were raided and the territory was targeted for major raids threatening all production, but the Winter Sun's presence blunted the attacks.
t.Kahraman: Fort Braydon's units intercepted a Jotun scout here. Probing attacks were expected to continue, but the fortification was enough to protect Kahraman provided the raids did not worsen.
t.Kallavesa: Jotun attacked halls in Kallavesa, and it was named as a target for major raids threatening every business, farm, forest, mine and herb garden until the Red Wind Corsairs blunted them.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold farmsteads were raided and probing attacks were expected to continue, but Forte Fidelis was sufficient to protect the territory provided the raids did not grow worse.
t.Mournwold: The Jotun raiders struck from the Mournwold and retreated back over the border into it after attacking Marcher farmsteads.
t.Sermersuaq: Halls in western Sermersuaq were attacked, but the Imperial armies stationed there cornered and wiped out two Jotun warbands and protected the territory.
t.Tassato: The city of Tassato stayed safe but its surrounding lands were plagued by raids. Major raids threatening its production were blunted by the Hounds of Glory.
t.Upwold: Upwold farmsteads were raided and the Eastern Guard was too far from the border to help, but the Fist of the Mountains was sent to blunt the major raids planned there.

r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named on the page, which only reports Jotun raids on Mitwold farmsteads and the protection of Forte Fidelis across the territory.

Sing a sad song.d: While the Golden Sun hunted the Druj through Holberg's forests, brightly coloured heralds of Lashonar came up the road from a Night regio in Axmure and infested its camps with a song of Glory, lost love and death. The song provoked sorrowful, contemplative moods rather than determination, which was dangerous against the Druj. Soldiers sought out congregations and comforts, and attendance rose in Holberg. Any army in the affected territory would lose 5% combat effectiveness, while congregations gained two extra votes and extra liao and every business gained 18 extra rings. The Golden Sun then moved to Spiral Castle in Weirwater, and the heralds followed, carrying both the harm and the benefits to that territory.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Golden Sun army was followed by Lashonar's heralds, and its soldiers' resolve was dulled by the song. The positive and negative effects were then felt across Dawnish Weirwater, where the army was being hosted at Spiral Castle.
n.Druj: The Druj were the foe the Golden Sun was hunting in Holberg, and the song's sorrowful effect on Imperial morale threatened to weaken the armies facing them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are not involved; the only link is the name Spiral Castle, a Dawnish noble seat in Weirwater where the Golden Sun was staying.
n.The League: Lashonar's song first spread among the Golden Sun's camps in League-held Holberg, where attendance at the territory's congregations crept upwards as soldiers sought comfort for their souls.

t.Holberg: The Golden Sun was hunting the Druj through Holberg's forests when the heralds arrived, and congregation attendance in the territory rose as soldiers contemplated their likely deaths, until the army moved on to Weirwater.
t.Semmerholm: The heralds of Lashonar issued forth from a Night regio somewhere in Semmerholm's region of Axmure before travelling up the road to Holberg.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the territory itself is not involved; the page refers only to Spiral Castle in Weirwater, where the Golden Sun was enjoying noble hospitality.
t.Weirwater: With the Golden Sun lodged at Spiral Castle, the heralds' song spread across Weirwater. Armies there would lose 5% combat effectiveness, while congregations would gain two extra votes and extra liao and every business 18 extra rings.

r.Semmerholm/Axmure: A Night regio somewhere in the depths of Axmure was the source of the stream of bird-heralds of Lashonar that went on to join the Golden Sun.

Strange allies.d: Scouts in the Brass Coast saw smoke and carrion crows across the border, and Faraden merchants reported Jotun legions from Narkyst burning south. The Iron Confederacy, under the Duke called the Grey Wolf, attacked Kalino, and Suranni merchants at the Sarvos embassy justified it as protecting trade. Juevar of the Hierro and a Lasambrian general came to Anvil seeking aid. Gudmundur Arason, King of Narkyst, warned that helping the Lasambrians would break the treaty. The civil service would not support the Lasambrians without Senate instruction. The Senate abrogated the Jotun ceasefire and agreed military support against the Jotun in northern Lasambria. Nothing more was heard from the south.

n.Jotun: Jotun hosts from Narkyst invaded northern Lasambria, and their King warned that Imperial aid to the Lasambrians would end the treaty; the Senate then abrogated that ceasefire.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun King cited Navarr working 'cursed magics' in Jotun lands as one of two earlier breaches of the treaty.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast scouts reported the fighting across the border, the Lasambrian delegation entered the Empire through Segura, and the Freeborn were divided between old grief over Lasambrian raids and the wish to befriend those who come in peace.
n.The League: Suranni merchants visiting the newly completed embassy in Sarvos argued the Iron Confederacy's case and were surprised the Empire cared about Lasambria's fate.

t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: carrion crows over the fighting were seen from the western woods of Serra Damata.
t.Kalino: Iron Confederacy soldiers under the Grey Wolf attacked the southern Lasambrian hills here; no chance arose to help the defenders, and no further news came.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: crows were seen from Beacon Point, and a Jotun Jarl spoke of her clan fighting in the West Ranging for over a year.
t.Reinos: Faraden merchants crossing the Reinos hills reported Jotun legions burning and killing their way south, and the Senate agreed to send military support against the Jotun in northern Lasambria.
t.Sarvos: Suranni merchants came to the new embassy in Sarvos to defend the Iron Confederacy's attack on the Lasambrians.
t.Segura: The Lasambrian delegation crossed Segura's western plains under a flag of truce, and Segurans were divided between memories of the Lasambrian invasion and the recent concord.

r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Mentioned in passing: a cloud of carrion crows over the fighting was seen from its western woods.
r.Liathaven/Beacon Point: Mentioned in passing: a great cloud of carrion crows was seen from Beacon Point.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: Mentioned in passing: a Jotun Jarl noted that her clan had been fighting in the West Ranging for over a year.
r.Segura/Burnish: Mentioned in passing: pillars of black smoke from the Lasambrian war were visible from Burnish.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Mentioned in passing: pillars of black smoke from the fighting were visible from Yellow Chase.

Trade winds.d: After the Senate placed the Imperial embassy to Jarm in Rigia, the eastern princes gained trade with the Empire, though the port was still unprepared for the influx. The northern and southern factions blamed Imperial interference and resented rumours of secret orc slave dealing, so captains met cold receptions in Kavor and bureaucratic obstruction in Vezak. The Commonwealth introduced tariffs on Imperial goods, citing the Empire's friendship with Jarm and its lack of interest in diplomacy with them, and might in theory close its ports. In Zemeh the Sumaah were openly hostile over Imperial ties to Asavea. Meanwhile Grendel Salt Lords gathered warships to harass and destroy Imperial vessels, making raiding less profitable.

n.Grendel: The Salt Lords massed their warships to patrol the southern bay and actively hunt Imperial ships, carrying heavily armed marines that made raids on Grendel shipping costly and less profitable.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the story's captain sails the Meade Minstrel carrying flour from the mills of Upwold, which was held up by Jarmish inspectors in Vezak.

t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel warships gathered in force in the southern waters of the bay, harassing and seeking to destroy Imperial ships, making engagements with Grendel vessels more dangerous than usual.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: flour from Upwold's mills formed part of a cargo that Jarmish officials in Vezak demanded be inspected for pests.

Unmade trove.d: Drusa found between 800 and 900 boxes of finely made mage implements, apparently preserved by a winter ritual. The find raised fresh questions about whether the Unmade Spire had planned to raise an army. The civil service calculated that 150 further mithril could make the Citadel Guard a large army in two seasons rather than a year. Alternatively, the cache could be gifted or sold to another nation, or worked with ilium to enhance the Army of the Citadel. The trove belonged to Urizen and was assigned like a national appointment. In the end Probus provided 25 rings of ilium to use the trove for enchantments after the Autumn Equinox 379YE.

n.Urizen: The trove legally belonged to Urizen, to be assigned by Senate motion or a unanimous decision of its senators. It offered the Citadel Guard faster growth or new enchantments, and was ultimately committed to enchantments with Probus's ilium.

t.Redoubt: The long mystery of the Unmade Spire's ruins in Redoubt deepened when a hidden chamber of preserved mage weapons and armour was uncovered there, prompting new theories about the spire's intentions.

r.Redoubt/Tomari: The map places here the discovery of the vaulted chamber beneath the Unmade Spire ruins, where hundreds of boxes of battle mage regalia had been preserved by a winter ritual.

Unwelcome guest.d: Acting on stories of a vallorn encroachment, General Cuth sent the Unconquered scouts attached to the Seventh Wave to investigate. With good information from the Suns of Couros and others, they found the infestation in a burgeoning Spring regio and spent several days mapping its extent. Judging it well within their ability, the general had the army surround the area and attack, with heavily armoured cataphracts cutting through the foliage and the husks within. Imperial magicians then confirmed that no trace of the vallorn remained. Left alone for a decade or two, it might have taken root. Two strange pods were presented to the Conclave. Later vallorn-related troubles in Casinea appeared unconnected to this incident.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a soldier remarks that the Pillar and the Pegasus are fighting the Druj in Reikos at the time.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Seventh Wave cleared a vallorn infestation from Highguard land at a cost of over ninety casualties, helped by information from the Suns of Couros.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a cataphract grumbles that the vallorn ought to be the Navarr's problem to deal with, and his comrades mock him for it.

t.Casinea: A vallorn encroachment in a Spring regio in Casinea was found and wholly destroyed before it could take root. Later vallorn-related problems in the territory appeared to have no link to it.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Pillar and the Pegasus are said to be in Reikos, deep in fighting against the Druj.

Wolf in summer.d: Shortly after the Spring Equinox, Sarvos, Temeschwar, Tassato and Holberg were all struck by a malaise. It left people lethargic, restless or aggressive, and brawls and ill-considered duels led to several deaths. An unusual heatwave with no wind and little rain made matters worse and raised fears of fire. Every mana site in League territories produced only half its usual crystalline mana, sending prices soaring, and several weak regio collapsed, one causing severe injuries. Divinations identified the curse, which must have been cast from within the Empire, through the Anvil regio or Winter regio in each territory. Who cast it was unknown, though some blamed Agramant. The effects faded after the Summer Solstice and did not recur.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a troupe leader in the story pours a Black Unicorn vintage white wine from Dawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: years of fighting the Druj are blamed for the dreadful state of Holberg's sewers, which worsened the heat there.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun raids are noted as an added worry in Tassato, where low river levels raised fears about fighting fires.
n.The League: Every League city suffered the curse and the heatwave, and League magicians, from troupe dramaturgists to street mages, saw their mana sources halved until the Solstice, while the culprit remained unknown.

t.Holberg: Holberg was hit especially hard, its war-neglected sewers and the stench of the Morass making the heat unbearable while its mana sites yielded only half their usual crystals.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos endured one of its worst summers on record, with people collapsing in the streets, drinking water being sold and brawls over crowded street tables, while its mana production was halved by the curse.
t.Tassato: In Tassato only the river kept the city from rioting, yet it fell to its lowest level since 296YE, exposing things better left submerged and raising fears that there would not be enough water to fight a major fire.
t.Temeschwar: Even usually mild Temeschwar saw soaring temperatures, and its mana sites, including well-kept forest estates, produced only half their normal crystals.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Those who could afford to were leaving Holfried for the Summer, seeking cooler climates away from the heat, failing sewers and the smell of the Morass.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Mentioned in passing: a mean little cellar in Tassato Mestra is cited as an example of how even humble mana sites were halved by the curse.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the curse and heatwave affected Tassato as a whole.
